skill.name: analyzing-patterns
skill.description: Analyze codebases for design patterns, architecture patterns, repeated structures, naming conventions, and maintainability anti-patterns.
skill.summary: Finds recurring code and architecture patterns, then turns them into practical refactoring guidance.

content.value_statement: Large codebases hide repeated structures and unclear architecture choices. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through systematic pattern analysis.
actual_capabilities: Identifies common design patterns such as Factory, Singleton, Observer, Strategy, Repository, Decorator, and Adapter.
Maps architectural styles including MVC, MVVM, layered architecture, microservices, event-driven design, and hexagonal architecture.
Guides searches for repeated code structures, naming conventions, import patterns, and file organization patterns.
Provides a Python detector that scans local source files for common pattern signatures.
Produces structured pattern reports with locations, intent, quality assessment, and refactoring suggestions.
Highlights common anti-patterns such as God objects, spaghetti code, copy-paste programming, and tight coupling.
limitations: Pattern detection is heuristic and can miss implicit designs without clear names or signatures.
The automated script reports candidate files, but it does not prove correct pattern implementation.
Architectural recommendations still need human review for product context and team constraints.
Some referenced helper resources are listed as planned or unavailable in this package.

use_cases.title: Review a Legacy Codebase
use_cases.description: Identify dominant patterns, inconsistent abstractions, and refactoring opportunities before planning modernization work.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Code Review
use_cases.description: Find repeated structures, naming conventions, and anti-patterns that deserve focused review comments.

use_cases.title: Learn an Unknown Project
use_cases.description: Build a concise map of architecture layers, data flow, and common implementation patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Find Basic Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a small project
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this project for common design patterns. List each pattern, its files, and why it appears to be used.

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Map the architecture of this codebase. Identify layers, data flow, boundaries, strengths, and areas that need improvement.

prompt_templates.title: Detect Repetition
prompt_templates.prompt: Find repeated code structures and naming conventions. Separate healthy consistency from duplication that should be refactored.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Refactoring
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a large codebase
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze design patterns, architecture patterns, and anti-patterns. Prioritize refactoring actions by impact, effort, and risk.

output_examples.input: Analyze the project architecture and identify major patterns.
output_examples.output: A report describing layered architecture, repository usage, service boundaries, data flow, strengths, risks, and targeted recommendations.

output_examples.input: Find repeated code patterns in the application.
output_examples.output: A duplication summary that groups similar validation, fetching, and transformation patterns with suggested extraction points.

output_examples.input: What design patterns are used in this codebase?
output_examples.output: A pattern inventory covering likely Factory, Observer, Strategy, and Singleton usage with file locations and quality notes.

best_practices: Run analysis on a focused project directory before expanding to the full repository.
Confirm each detected pattern by reading the implementation, not only by matching names.
Prioritize recommendations that reduce maintenance cost or clarify architecture boundaries.
anti_patterns: Do not force a design pattern when simpler code is clearer.
Do not treat every repeated structure as harmful duplication.
Do not run helper scripts on unrelated system directories.

faq.question: Does this skill change source code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides analysis and recommendations. Any code changes require a separate user request.

faq.question: Can it detect every design pattern?
faq.answer: No. It detects common indicators and provides a review process. Subtle patterns need manual confirmation.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What languages does the detector cover?
faq.answer: The included script scans common TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, Go, and Rust extensions.

faq.question: Is this useful for refactoring planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It connects repeated patterns and anti-patterns to practical refactoring recommendations.

faq.question: Should I trust automated results without review?
faq.answer: No. Treat automated findings as candidates, then verify intent and implementation quality.
